question.:question/problem: Calculate $\int \frac{1}{4x+6}\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, let $u=4x+6.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{4x+6}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+6|+C\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the above by writing $C=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡K$ for another arbitrary constant $K,$ and then we can combine the two terms using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+6|+C & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+6|+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+6|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|4x+6|)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we finally conclude that

$$
\int \frac{1}{4x+6}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|4x+6|).
$$

question.:question/problem: Calculate $\int \frac{1}{4-3x}\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, let $u=4-3x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{4-3x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot (-\frac{1}{3})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-3x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the above by writing $C=-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡K$ for another arbitrary constant $K,$ and then we can combine the two terms using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-3x|+C & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-3x|-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-3x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K) \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|4-3x|)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we finally conclude that

$$
\int \frac{1}{4-3x}\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|4-3x|).
$$
